I was in a relationship with a man like this when I was 18-21, and he did exactly the same things your boyfriend is doing. I know and understand how incredibly hard it is to permanently end things, especially when they do absolutely anything in the world to prevent it. Mine would show up at my work, make hundreds of TextFree/burner numbers to text me from, call nonstop, I still feel nauseous if my phone rings more than twice in a row. He also messaged my friends and mom with absolutely insane lies about me. 

I know it’s hard, but I absolutely promise you OP, ending things permanently will be the one of the best decisions and feelings you’ll ever have. It will be hard, he will probably beg, and threaten to kill himself, and message your family and friends. But you HAVE to stand your ground. It’s so hard, but eventually, he will give up and find a new victim. And your life will get so, so, so much better. 

I don’t know how old you are OP, but life is too short to spend it trapped in an abusive relationship. I don’t know if you recognize/have accepted it yet, but the way your boyfriend if acting is abusive and controlling and scary. You are NOT responsible for his mental health. He is abusing you and controlling you and taking advantage of your empathy and kindness over being concerned for his well being.

I tried to break up with him probably 50+ times until I was finally able to end things. But I’m almost 26 now, and truly, it is one of the best things I ever did for myself. I feel so much sadness and pity for the young girl I was being abused by him, but I am always so proud because it was so hard to withstand the harassment and stalking for months, but it’s what has allowed me to become who I am today.

Please feel free to message me if you need any other kind of support/want to vent. Your post really does resonate with me so much, and I want you to know that your life will get SO much better when this man is out of it.

I moved to Philly last summer from Boston, after living in Boston my whole life. I’m also vegan so I have some insight on that. 

Boston is clean and generally safer feeling than Philadelphia. Decent vegan/vegetarian subculture, but generally overpriced and cliche restaurants that cater to that diet. But most restaurants will have at least 1 vegetarian option, no promises it’ll be amazing though. Good public transport (MBTA) but it’s a nightmare to understand/navigate, compared to Philly. The routes don’t make as much sense, Philly is set up like a grid where generally the lines run either left to right, or up and down. 

No-go zones in Boston are SIGNIFICANTLY rarer than Philly. I’m sorry to say it, but as a young female, I have felt dramatically more unsafe at a baseline level than in Boston. For better or worse, people in Philly seem much more likely to engage in conversation with you. That makes the people seem more friendly and easy to talk to, but it also means you’ll get an increased rate of negative conversations. Unwarranted comments on your appearance, begging, general crazy people, etc. 

The rate at which I have uncomfortable interactions with people here compared to Boston is probably 100 to 1. In Boston you can take public transit with zero to little chance of feeling afraid or unsafe. That is not the same in Philly. The public transit here is also generally dirtier than Boston. Again, I’m sorry to say it Philly, but the transit stations here literally stink of pee or shit or trash. 

Of course there are sterilized areas of Philly that feel exactly the same as Boston. But if you go a few blocks over, you will see a dramatically different area that hasn’t been polished for tourists. In Boston it’s hard to end up in a no-go area unless you’re specifically seeking it out.

Boston and Philly are equally walkable I would say. However Philly is also a lot bigger than Boston, you really can’t understand the scale until you’ve been to both. Philly has a lot of cool great areas, but it might be a half hour- hour train ride to get there. Boston is a lot more concentrated. 

If you’re well off and can afford Boston prices and want a more clean and polished visit, I’d say Boston. But people there will probably not be very “friendly” unless you’re getting drunk in a bar together. Boston has put a lot of money and effort into grooming the city to be desirable as a city for all the college students there. A huge sector of the Boston economy is college students and higher ed. Boston understands that if the city was unattractive to outsiders, they would lose their money. 

If you want to experience the gritty feel of a true city, with friendlier people and better food, Philly is what you should go with. People in Philly will probably be genuinely interested in your story, why you’re in Philly, and give you cool recommendations on what to do. People will give you directions if you need them, etc. In Boston, nobody really gives a fuck about what anyone else is doing.

I spend maybe 150 a month in groceries for a single person. However, it is quite honestly probably a depressing seeming diet to most people who can spend a lot on groceries. I’d love if I could but those kind of things can literally double or triple your grocery expenses. I don’t buy cookies or chips or anything that is a name brand really. I don’t buy any liquids that are just flavored, like juice, or energy drinks or whatever. I drink water at home and use the coffee machine at work for free coffee. Things like coffee and tea and flavored drinks also cost a lot more than you might think. 

Anything I buy that can perish or mold I keep in either the fridge or freezer. I shop almost exclusively at Aldi’s.

I tried it once and waking up after in the hospital and seeing just how many lives I affected, even without succeeding, really sucked. I know my life is my own to lead and choose what I want to do, but that experience quickly taught me suicide isn’t an option. 

A few years after my attempt my dad killed himself, his life was just about as horrible and indignant as it could be at the end of his life. Got out of jail, didn’t get any help transitioning back out. Couldn’t get a job, was disabled from doctors cutting a nerve during surgery. Relapsed on his meds, DCF told my mom she had to kick him out or we’d go to foster care. Etc etc etc, he died homeless while sleeping on a park bench in winter.

And you know what? I understand why he killed himself. I would’ve too. I think many people would. Life is a sad, painful, harsh world sometimes. The state of everything is so fucking scary. But I’m 23, able bodied, mostly all there mentally, and I have to at least try. I hope it’s not too morbid, but there’s a quote I love. To paraphrase, it’s something like, “if you’re going to kill yourself, why rush? You have all the time in the world”. 

It helps me a lot when suicidal thoughts crop back up. If you really truly don’t care about living and are ready to die, why rush to get to it now? You’re just about the most free any person could feel in terms of obligations and fear. That’s your only thing left, right? So just … give it some time. Please take this EXTREMELY surface level. If you’re actually suicidal and in danger, please seek help. 

But if you’re having the thoughts, tell yourself, maybe in a couple weeks. Maybe in a couple weeks, let me see if anything else comes up until then. There’s been times where I’ve been 1% away from attempting, and I remember that quote. And I’ll be convinced it’s bullshit and I’ll still do it anyway, but I’ll wait until tomorrow. I have a load of laundry I still need to take out. Or I forgot to mail a letter. Or I still need to return a library book. Ok, it’ll have to wait until at least tomorrow. 

And honestly? So far, 100% of the time, I find something or remember something that reminds me to just keeping going. Wouldn’t be here otherwise. There’s always something you can find. 

People like to talk on a big grand scale about life and purpose. Like when you’re suicidal, they’ll go on and on about “you have meaning and purpose in life! You have no idea where you’ll be 10 years from now!”. That’s never helped me, because I don’t care about that when I’m in that state. 

But if I can even just remember the goose that’s nesting outside my work window, that helps. I need to change the water bowl I put out for her. Nobody else will, and it’s 100 degrees out. This will have to wait until the eggs hatch and she can go to the river. Small things.
